title: Coastal States Bank Announces Charlie Labassi as Treasury Services Relationship Banker
summary: Coastal States Bank (“CSB”), a local community bank, announces Charlie Labassi as Treasury Services Relationship Banker
body_text: HILTON HEAD ISLAND, SC / CHARLESTON, SC / SAVANNAH, GA / (February 18, 2026) – Coastal States Bank (“CSB”) announced that Charlie Labassi has joined the community bank as Treasury Services Relationship Banker serving its Coastal regional markets across the Lowcountry and Savannah. Specializing in analyzing and improving treasury processes for businesses, Labassi brings more than 20 years of corporate treasury and banking experience to his role at CSB. As Treasury Services Relationship Banker, Labassi will partner with businesses in Hilton Head, Bluffton, Beaufort, Charleston and Savannah to deliver efficient, technology-driven treasury solutions and help companies streamline financial operations, enhance cash flow management and reduce costs. “We’re excited to have Charlie join CSB,” said Brian Smith, CSB’s Coastal Regional President. “His extensive experience and consultative approach align with our commitment to deliver relationship-based banking and help businesses in our communities operate efficiently for long-term success.” Labassi is an active member of the community and supporter of local environmental initiatives, currently serving as a member of The Turtle Trackers on Hilton Head Island, which aids endangered sea turtles in the Lowcountry. About the Company Coastal States Bank builds relationships by providing a full range of banking services designed for businesses, their owners and individuals looking for a local banking partner. CSB has a community banking presence in Savannah, the Lowcountry of South Carolina (Hilton Head Island, Bluffton and Beaufort) and the Atlanta Metropolitan market and serves communities across the country through its Government Guaranteed Lending, Senior Housing, Correspondent Marine and Mortgage Banker Finance lines of business. At present, CSB has approximately $2.3 billion in total assets. CSB is a wholly-owned subsidiary of CoastalSouth Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: COSO). Coastal States Bank – Local. And Proud of It.® For additional information regarding Coastal States Bank, please visit www.coastalstatesbank.com . ### Media Contact: Raquel Cobb VP, Marketing and Communications Director Coastal States Bank [email protected]

title: 7 Best HVAC scheduling software tools in 2026
summary: Find the 7 best HVAC scheduling software tools for 2026. We compare pricing, features, and reviews to help you find the right fit.
body_text: Many HVAC businesses start out managing schedules with a mix of spreadsheets, phone calls, text messages, and paper notes. That might work when you’re running a few jobs a day. But disjointed systems create extra work by requiring manual updates every time a job changes. As you grow, these tasks add up fast, pulling your team away from more valuable work. Investing in HVAC scheduling software is how you can get a handle on the chaos. These tools bring scheduling, dispatching, customer information, and technician updates into one place. Some platforms can also integrate with your business phone software to automate customer notifications via text message. This way, you can reduce no-shows and keep schedules on track. Below, we’ll walk you through seven of the best software solutions for HVAC scheduling. We looked at their features, pricing, strengths, and limitations to help you find the right fit for your business. 7 Best HVAC scheduling software researched and ranked Below is a comparison of the top seven HVAC scheduling software tools. Find out what they do, how much they cost, and which one best fits your team. 7 Best HVAC software for scheduling compared Here’s an overview of the best scheduling software for HVAC businesses: Provider Starting price Best for Standout features Jobber $29 per month for one user Small and growing HVAC businesses Client hub, GPS tracking and route optimization, online booking, automated reminders FieldPulse Custom pricing Workflow automation and customization Workflow automation, AI dispatcher, route optimization, multiple dispatch views Housecall Pro $59 per month HVAC-specific integrations Bluon equipment lookup, employee GPS tracking, HVAC financing, review management Workyard $6 per user per month, scheduling requires an upgrade Time tracking and labor management Geofenced GPS time tracking, mileage tracking, labor cost reporting, job costing FieldEdge Custom pricing Maintenance agreement management Maintenance agreement management, real-time dispatch board, two-way QuickBooks sync Service Fusion Custom pricing Teams that need unlimited users Unlimited users, customer portal, online booking, flat-rate pricing ServiceTitan Custom pricing Large HVAC companies AI-powered technician recommendations, online booking, capacity planning, advanced reporting 1. Jobber: Best HVAC scheduling software for small and growing businesses Pros Appointment booking and reminders Online self-scheduling Customer-facing client portal Automatic mapping and routing Job tracking and dispatch alerts Cons Team plans have user minimums that can raise the price Jobber is an ‌ HVAC business software that helps you manage scheduling and dispatching from a single calendar. You can see technician availability, job locations, and incoming service requests in one view. When an emergency call comes in, you can see which technician is nearby and drag the job straight onto their timeline. You can keep jobs that are waiting on parts or customer confirmation in a sidebar and add them to the calendar later. On the Grow and Plus plans, the Find a Time feature suggests appointment slots based on technician availability and drive time. Here’s how one business owner described their experience with Jobber’s scheduling tools: “ I like that Jobber is really easy to use both on the computer in the office and [in] the field, which makes my work much easier. The clients can sign, we can bill, and they can pay on-site, all seamlessly. The easy-to-use scheduling dashboard allows us to reassign technicians to tasks and reschedule customers effortlessly. ” — G2 The software also helps reduce time on the road by mapping the most efficient routes for your team. Technicians can view their schedules, update job statuses, and access customer data from the mobile app. They also receive alerts about schedule changes and cancellations as they happen. Through Jobber’s fleet management partners, you can track vehicle locations, fuel levels, and idling time. Jobber also integrates with Quo, the best business phone system for HVAC teams. Once it’s set up, Quo’s call summaries and transcripts show up automatically on the right customer record in Jobber. Whoever picks up the phone next knows what was discussed, even if they weren’t the one who took the original call. You can also use click-to-call to reach customers with a single tap from their Jobber contact card, using your Quo business number. If your team is unavailable to pick up, turn on Sona , Quo’s 24/7 HVAC answering service , to stop losing potential customers to missed calls. Sona follows your custom instructions to collect the caller’s details, equipment issue, and job urgency. You can also instruct it to set up a service request in Jobber based on the conversation and your requirements. Key features of Jobber QuickBooks integration for accounting and invoicing Mobile app for field crews Automated vehicle fleet tracking Smart “Find a Time” opening locator Vehicle health and performance management Jobber pricing Jobber offers pricing plans for solopreneurs, starting at $29 per month billed annually. Otherwise, their pricing depends on how many users you have. Here are their tiers for teams of up to five people: Connect: $149 per month for up to five users for job scheduling, the client hub for job history, checklists, GPS tracking with route optimization, automated invoicing and payments, and QuickBooks/Xero sync Grow: $229 per month for two-way SMS, job costing, automatic time tracking, and custom workflow automations Plus: $399 per month for a built-in AI receptionist for handling inbound calls and bookings, lead pipeline tracking, the full marketing suite, and premium support. 2. FieldPulse: Best HVAC scheduling software with workflow automation Pros Visual route planning with built-in route optimization Multiple dispatch board views for busy schedules Built-in technician commission tracking Offline mode Cons Pricing requires a custom quote Some users report occasional delays with QuickBooks syncing QuickBooks integration requires an upgrade FieldPulse is an HVAC management software solution for growing service businesses. Like Jobber, it combines scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, and customer management in one platform. You’ll get a drag-and-drop calendar and can use GPS tracking and route optimization to dispatch the closest tech to a job. There’s also a mobile app to help keep your field teams aligned. Need to track scheduling efficiency, technician workloads, and dispatch performance? FieldPulse offers reporting tools to make that happen. You can even use historical data to forecast busy seasons so you staff smarter. What sets FieldPulse apart is the depth of its business management tools. You can sync field and accounting data with QuickBooks Desktop without relying on manual exports. You can also track individual HVAC units by serial number, warranty information, and service history. For sales teams, FieldPulse includes a built-in pipeline that helps manage leads and estimates. “ I switched over from Jobber. I am new to the platform but, so far, the quickbooks sync seems to be working as needed. The quality of the estimate portion of the program allows me to put a better package together to allow the customer to make an informed decision. It is also a time saver in the field for the techs to invoice. ” — G2 Key features of FieldPulse Good-Better-Best proposal builder Equipment and asset tracking with service history Flat-rate pricebook for consistent pricing Custom forms and inspection checklists FieldPulse pricing FieldPulse doesn’t publicly disclose its pricing. You’ll need to contact their sales team for a quote. Teams can choose from three FieldPulse plans: Essentials: Custom pricing for customer management, scheduling and dispatching, work order management, estimates and invoicing, the mobile app, and workflow automation Professional: Custom pricing for project management and QuickBooks integration Enterprise: Custom pricing for multi-location management and API access 3. HouseCall Pro: Best for HVAC-specific integrations Pros HVAC integrations with Bluon and Profit Rhino Vehicle GPS with dashcam monitoring Bilingual mobile app for English- and Spanish-speaking crews Cons Adding additional users requires upgrading your plan QuickBooks syncing isn’t included on every plan Mobile app lacks offline editing Housecall Pro is an HVAC field service management software . It makes scheduling easier with a drag-and-drop calendar. You can schedule one-time or recurring visits and update appointments as needed. For larger projects, you can assign multiple technicians to the same job and split the work across multiple appointments. There’s also a live technician map that makes it easy to manage dispatching and improve customer communication. Housecall Pro also connects with HVAC-specific tools like Bluon and Profit Rhino. With the Bluon integration, your technicians can scan a unit’s data plate right inside the Housecall Pro mobile app to view: Model specifications and estimated warranty information OEM manuals and wiring diagrams Part specifications Compatible replacement parts OEM part numbers and known aftermarket replacements You can also use this tool to have your technicians create estimates, send invoices, and accept payments from the field. Automated payment reminders help reduce follow-up work on unpaid invoices. Keep in mind that Housecall Pro limits you to a single user on the base plan. If you switch to the mid-tier plan, that cap increases to five users. Even on the highest plan, you can only have up to eight users. If your crew expands past that point, you’ll have to pay for additional users, which costs an extra $35 per person per month. Here’s what one business owner had to say about Housecall Pro’s pricing model: “ I do not like having to pay more to add more contractors. I would prefer to not do that, as I will be adding more over the next year, and it significantly increases my pricing. ” — G2 Key features of HouseCall Pro Good-Better-Best on-site proposals Built-in Wisetack financing for high-ticket jobs Smart scheduling based on drive time and route logic 24/7 online booking via website or Google Automated customer texts with live GPS tech tracking HouseCall Pro pricing HouseCall Pro lets you choose from three pricing plans: Basic: $59 per month for one user for scheduling and dispatching, quotes and proposals, invoices and payments, online booking, review management, job cost tracking, a price book, mobile app, and offline viewing Essentials: $149 per month for up to five users for QuickBooks online and desktop sync, postcards and email marketing, customer equipment tracking, premium review management, a visual price book, employee GPS tracking, and checklists MAX: $299 per month for up to eight users for advanced custom reporting, a dedicated onboarding specialist, and escalated phone support, with extra users at $35 per user per month 4. Workyard: Best HVAC scheduling software with prevailing-wage compliance Pros Comprehensive time and mileage management features Detailed job costing Low monthly cost per user Offers an offline mode Cons Scheduling features require upgrading to the mid-tier plan Doesn’t offer estimates, quoting, or other accounting features Accounting integrations require an upgrade Workyard is workforce management software built to protect your payroll margins. It tracks employee hours, drive time, and labor costs, helping you spot payroll problems before they eat into your margins. You can use Workyard to schedule long-term project work, work orders, emergency calls, and recurring service visits. Assigning a job automatically links it to GPS and time tracking. This helps you stay on top of payroll, labor costs, and compliance reporting. Field crews can also upload photos and job notes directly from the app while they’re on-site. Your office gets a real-time view of job progress without having to chase technicians for updates. Here’s what a business owner had to say about Workyard: “ It is very efficient having all of our jobs and tasks in one place, with time, location, and team members assigned to each job. The initial setup was pretty seamless, and everyone adjusted and learned how to use the system pretty quickly. ” — G2 The downside is that scheduling only comes with the mid-tier Pro plan. Workyard’s Starter plan includes field management and GPS tracking, but it skips the calendar entirely. If you handle government or union contracts or lose money to unlogged overtime or buddy-punching, Workyard fits well. But know that you’ll need to budget more for scheduling features. Key features of Workyard Project-filtered scheduling views Task-linked compliance and labor codes Geofenced appointment verification logs Real-time task progress feeds One-click mobile schedule updates Workyard pricing Workyard offers three pricing plans based on how much functionality you need. Pricing starts at $6 per user per month, though scheduling tools are only available on the Pro plan and above. Here’s a quick breakdown: Starter: GPS time tracking, mileage tracking, live crew location tracking, payroll integrations, expense tracking, timesheet reporting, and notes, receipts, and photos Pro: Office-to-field scheduling, task management, recurring tasks, geofenced clock-ins, GPS arrival detection, labor cost tracking, mileage reporting, live dashboard, accounting integrations, and activity feed Enterprise: Custom pricing for teams of 50 or more that need ERP integrations, API access, automated data syncing, incident reporting, meal and rest break compliance, alert notifications, premium support, and dedicated onboarding assistance 5. FieldEdge: Best for native maintenance agreement management Pros Built-in maintenance agreement management Real-time dispatch and scheduling board Live two-way QuickBooks synchronization Cons Steeper learning curve than most competitors Dashboard lacks customization options Mobile app performance can be inconsistent FieldEdge is a real-time dispatch tool. That means it uses a live map to show where every truck is and what each technician is working on. When a new service call comes in, you just drag the job over to the closest technician on your screen, and the system sends the details to that tech’s phone. The software also includes location mapping and team management tools. Dispatchers can quickly reassign work when schedules change or an emergency call comes in. If a job requires multiple technicians, you can assign them to the same work order. FieldEdge also supports multi-day scheduling for larger installations and commercial projects. For businesses that rely on maintenance agreements, FieldEdge offers a native tracking system to help you stay on top of things. You can use it to track expiring agreements, upcoming renewals, and billing schedules. It also helps automate renewal notices, reducing the need for manual follow-ups. But FieldEdge isn’t the easiest platform to get started with. Multiple users say onboarding can feel difficult, and several note the QuickBooks integration can be glitchy or slow to sync. One business owner said: “ We got almost no support from field edge while using their software. We were often left to figure things out on our own. ” — Capterra Key features of FieldEdge Good-Better-Best multi-option quoting Integrated customer notification system Live two-way QuickBooks sync Built-in flat-rate pricebook with 30,000+ HVAC repair lines Mobile access to schedules, customer history, and payments FieldEdge pricing FieldEdge offers three plans for HVAC teams. The company doesn’t publicly disclose pricing, so you’ll need to contact its sales team for a custom quote. Here’s what each plan includes: Select: Booking and scheduling, dispatching, customer management and service history, technician time tracking, invoicing and payments, QuickBooks online and desktop sync, flat-rate pricing, and basic service agreements Premier: Advanced dispatching, advanced service agreements, multi-option quotes, prospect tracking, performance and commission tracking, saved reports, and additional mobile app licenses Elite: Professional sales proposal tools, unlimited saved reports, warehouse inventory management, outbound call recording, and a customer portal 6. Service Fusion: Best for flat-rate pricing with unlimited users Pros Flat-rate pricing with unlimited users Core features are included across all plans Customer portal for online bookings and service requests Cons No free trial is available Mobile app can be slow and prone to syncing issues Limited form and document customization Service Fusion is field service management software for HVAC and other home service businesses. It brings scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, estimates, and customer records into one system. The main scheduling features are fairly standard. You get a drag-and-drop calendar and can see technician schedules and drive times to reduce double bookings. You can also create dispatch zones for specific techs for more effective scheduling. What sets Service Fusion apart is its pricing model. Every plan includes unlimited users for a flat monthly fee. Scheduling, customer management, estimates, and reporting are also included in the base plan. However, there are a few areas where Service Fusion still leaves much to be desired. For example, you can get basic phone and texting tools with an upgrade. You can make calls and send messages, but the platform lacks features like advanced call routing and automated follow-ups. Due to the nature of all-in-one apps, the phone functionality lacks specialization and feels bolted on. It wouldn’t meet the needs of a growing HVAC business that relies on the phone to manage customer relationships and get jobs. The Service Fusion mobile app also receives its share of complaints. Some users report app crashes, freezing screens, and slow loading times. Others mention problems uploading photos or updating job information from the field. Here’s the experience of a business owner using Service Fusion to power their HVAC scheduling. “ Sometimes in the field, the usability and slower download speeds of the app are hard to learn. Mobile devices’ functionality could be slightly simpler, as it can be harder for older techs to understand. ” — G2 Key features of Service Fusion AI-powered technician dispatch recommendations Adaptive capacity planning Certification-based technician scheduling Online booking tied to live availability Automated schedule optimization Service Fusion pricing Service Fusion offers three pricing tiers to choose from: Starter: $208 per month for customer management, estimates and jobs, scheduling and dispatching, integrated payments, QuickBooks integration, invoicing, payment processing, project management, reporting, and text messaging alerts Plus: $325 per month for estimate options, job photo uploads, inventory management, job costing, and integrated voice and text Pro: $533 per month for open API integration, custom documents, eSign documents, customer web portal, and progress billing and recurring invoicing 7. ServiceTitan: Best for large HVAC companies Pros Supports residential and commercial HVAC operations AI-powered scheduling optimization and route planning Modern payment tools, including Tap to Pay Open API for custom integrations Cons Pricing isn’t publicly available Some users find the learning curve steep Some users report price jumps as add-ons start stacking ServiceTitan is field service management software for larger HVAC businesses. In addition to scheduling, it covers marketing, payments, customer management, and reporting. It offers everything an HVAC business team needs when they’re at scale. Dispatchers can tag jobs with important details to help technicians arrive at the job prepared. You can also organize upcoming jobs using custom tags. These make it easier to spot special customer needs and make sure your crew arrives prepared. For example, if a customer prefers to speak Spanish, you can add a “Spanish Speaker” tag so your office always sends the right technician for the job. Planning large installations and long-term work? You can view jobs weeks or even months in advance. You can also use ServiceTitan’s AI-powered dispatching tools to reduce the scheduling burden on your office staff. Set these up to automate technician assignments, calculate drive times, and match jobs with the right technicians. If you want customers to book their own appointments, ServiceTitan offers a premium add-on called Scheduling Pro. This is a 24/7 online scheduling tool built for the trades that gives homeowners a fast, mobile-first way to book jobs straight from their phones. You can embed it on various digital channels, including: Your company website Your official Google listing Your digital ads and links That said, ServiceTitan is one of the most expensive HVAC software options on the market. The vendor charges enterprise-level rates for most features and getting everything set up takes time. If you’re a smaller business just getting started, the cost may be hard to justify. Key features of ServiceTitan AI-powered technician recommendations Online booking tied to real-time availability Capacity planning tools for busy seasons Automatic job matching based on technician skills and certifications Mobile Tap-to-Pay payments ServiceTitan pricing ServiceTitan uses custom pricing based on your business needs. HVAC companies can choose from three tiers: Starter: Scheduling, dispatching, call booking, invoicing, and pricebook management Essentials: Mobile estimates and payroll management The Works: Advanced reporting, commission tracking, configurable payroll, and membership management To find out what ServiceTitan will cost your team, reach out to its sales team for a quote. What features should I look for in HVAC scheduling software? Looking for scheduling software can be exhausting because there are so many tools out there. This list will help you cut through the noise and find what your business needs. Real-time field-to-office sync Office staff often have little idea what’s happening in the field until a tech calls in. A reliable HVAC scheduling app syncs work orders, job history, and live status updates. This keeps technicians and office staff on the same page all day. Integration with your business phone solution Calls are still the most common way customers book HVAC jobs. When your scheduling software links to your small business phone system , customer details appear before you pick up. Your team can see past jobs, equipment history, and call records at a glance. Open arrival slots, daily calendar grids, and nearby route zones are also visible right on the screen. Smart dispatch and scheduling Manually matching jobs to availability is slow and error-prone. Good HVAC scheduling software lets you assign jobs in real time based on technician location, skill set, and availability. Mobile access with offline functionality Your techs need to view their job details and appointment times, even when working in a basement with no signal. Look for a tool that keeps working offline and automatically syncs changes when the connection returns. Customer self-scheduling HVAC emergencies don’t wait for business hours. Make sure the tool you choose captures those late-night and weekend job requests while your office is closed. Maintenance agreement and recurring job scheduling Maintenance contracts are one of the steadiest revenue streams in HVAC. Choose software that sets up recurring visits, tracks active service agreements, and alerts you before a visit is overdue. Invoicing and accounting integrations The faster a job closes, the faster you get paid. Pick software that lets techs create HVAC estimates quickly and take payments in the field, with QuickBooks sync built in. Reporting and job costing It’s hard to know if a job made money without tracking labor and material costs. The best tools break down revenue by technician, job type, or service area and compare labor, parts, and time against what you billed. Our scoring system for the top HVAC scheduling software options explained To identify the top seven HVAC scheduling software providers, we first created a scoring system. Here’s why and how we use this scoring system to rank the best performing tools for your business: Why we used a scoring system. It’s difficult to compare software providers in-depth across all categories. This scoring system helps to simplify the process by assigning an honest, objective score to each one. We look at the same areas. We evaluated each HVAC scheduling software provider using the same key areas, which we discuss in more detail below. This ensures a fair comparison and removes personal bias from the scores. One final score. We calculated an overall score for each platform to better determine which ones should rank among the top seven. This also makes it easier for you to compare multiple platforms at a glance. What we evaluated We looked at the following seven key areas: Ease of use. We factored in how long the platform takes to set up, as well as the technician mobile app experience. Essential HVAC scheduling features. We looked at features like smart dispatch, routing, and maintenance agreements. We also checked for a live field-to-office sync, offline mobile access, and full equipment histories. Finally, we looked at how each tool handles emergency calls by letting you slot in urgent jobs, reassign techs on the fly, and notify customers. Scheduling and dispatch. We watched for automations with appointment scheduling, estimates, and customer follow-ups. Integrations. We evaluated connections with tools like phone solutions, accounting software, and CRMs . Customer support. We looked at support channels, hours, and user feedback. Pricing transparency. We considered pricing, hidden fees, add-ons, and upgrade requirements. Company reputation. We checked out reviews, trial availability, and subscription tiers. How scoring works Each platform received a score from 0 to 10 based on its performance across the seven key areas mentioned above. Here are the score ranges: Score Range Meaning 9.0 – 10.0 One of the best options available 7.5 – 8.9 Very strong performance with minor limitations 6.0 – 7.4 Average performance 3.0 – 5.9 Significant limitations 1.0 – 2.9 Poor performance 0 Feature not available How we calculate overall scores Not every software feature carries the same weight. Some tools have a bigger impact on your daily cash flow, technician adoption, and growth capacity. Here’s how much each area contributes to the final score: Evaluation factor Weight Ease of use 25% Field service management features 40% Integrations 15% Customer support 10% Pricing transparency 5% Company reputation 5% We calculate the final score using this formula: Final score = (each area’s score out of 10 × its % importance), then add everything together. Complete your HVAC stack with the right business phone The best HVAC scheduling software keeps your calendar organized and your team aligned. But even the best scheduling tool won’t help if customers can’t reach you in the first place. HVAC jobs are won and lost in the moments people are trying to get through, like during an emergency, when calling to confirm an appointment, or when they’re comparing you to the next business on Google. Your phone setup is the front door to everything your scheduling software manages behind it. That means the right business phone solution isn’t an afterthought — it’s part of the same operational stack. Look for a VoIP system that keeps calls, voicemails, and texts in one place and lets any dispatcher pick up a conversation from a shared inbox. It should also connect to your scheduling software so your team has full context before a tech steps on-site. To find the right fit for your HVAC business, read our full guide on VoIP for HVAC companies. FAQs What is HVAC scheduling software? HVAC scheduling software helps schedule jobs, assign technicians, and keep service appointments organized. It gives you and your team one shared schedule with live field-to-office updates. Many tools also include dispatching, time tracking, and invoicing to help you bill accurately for every job. What is the best HVAC software? The best HVAC scheduling software depends on your business size and needs. Quo is the best business phone system for HVAC companies. Jobber is ideal for growing teams that want a simple scheduling system. FieldPulse is better if you need flexible workflows and custom fields. Larger businesses should consider ServiceTitan for enterprise-level business management. What’s the difference between HVAC scheduling software and field service management software? HVAC scheduling software handles scheduling, dispatch, and job assignments. It tracks open time slots, sends appointment reminders, and assigns calls to your technicians. HVAC field service management software is a broader category. It covers scheduling features, as well as tools for estimating, invoicing, and customer management. Some platforms also offer inventory management and reporting as part of the same system. What are the benefits of cloud HVAC software? Some of the main reasons contractors invest in cloud HVAC software include: – Increased flexibility. Technicians and dispatchers can view and update schedules from any device. – Fewer communication gaps. Changes sync instantly between the office and the field, so everyone works from the latest information. – Faster billing. Techs can access service history and send invoices before leaving the job site. – Better customer experience. Cloud software makes it easier for leads and customers to stay in touch and book appointments. Some tools even let them receive invoices and pay online. How much does HVAC scheduling software cost? HVAC scheduling software starts at around $6 per user per month and can exceed $100 per month for more advanced platforms. Costs vary based on your team size and the features you need. Some providers only offer custom pricing, requiring you to contact their sales team for a quote. Is all-in-one HVAC software better than having multiple apps? It depends on your business. All-in-one HVAC software is easier to manage because everything works in one system. The downside is that many built-in features are less specialized. Specialized apps give you deeper features for accounting, customer communication, and job costing. The tradeoff is that your apps must integrate well to avoid manual work and data silos.

title: First Interstate Earns Silver Stevie Award for Corporate Social Responsibility
summary: We earned a Silver Stevie Award® for corporate social responsibility in the 2026 American Business Awards®, recognizing our people’s community impact across our footprint.
body_text: First Interstate was named a Silver Stevie Award® winner for Achievement in Corporate Social Responsibility in the 24th Annual American Business Awards®. The American Business Awards are the U.S.A.’s premier business awards program. All organizations operating in the U.S.A. are eligible to submit nominations — public and private, for-profit and nonprofit, large and small. Nicknamed the Stevies for the Greek word meaning “crowned,” the awards will be presented to winners at a gala ceremony at the Marriott Marquis Hotel in New York on Tuesday, June 9, 2026. “This recognition is a reflection of the thousands of employees across our footprint who invest their time, talent, and resources into the communities we call home,” said Amberly Pahut, Director of Community Responsibility. “From our Believe in Local grants to our annual Volunteer Day to the everyday acts of generosity our teams carry out year-round, corporate social responsibility isn’t just something we do — it’s part of who we are.” At a Glance 60,540+ employee volunteer hours in 2025 3,304 organizations supported through volunteerism $1 million in Believe in Local grants directed to 40 employee-nominated nonprofits $7.2 million+ in combined grants and donations from First Interstate and the First Interstate BancSystem Foundation in 2025 $100 million+ in philanthropic giving since 1990 Community Responsibility in Action Our commitment to community goes far beyond banking. In 2025, employees volunteered more than 60,540 hours across 3,304 organizations. Through our Believe in Local campaign, $1 million in grants were directed to 40 employee-nominated nonprofits addressing critical needs across our footprint. Together, First Interstate and the First Interstate BancSystem Foundation provided more than $7.2 million in grants and donations in 2025, bringing total philanthropic giving to more than $100 million since 1990. From hunger relief and financial education to winter clothing drives and disaster response, corporate social responsibility at First Interstate isn’t a program — it’s a culture carried out by our people every day. About the Stevie Awards Stevie Awards are conferred in nine programs: the Asia-Pacific Stevie Awards, the German Stevie Awards, the Middle East & North Africa Stevie Awards, The American Business Awards®, The International Business Awards®, the Stevie Awards for Women in Business, the Stevie Awards for Great Employers, the Stevie Awards for Sales & Customer Service, and the Stevie Awards for Technology Excellence. Stevie Awards competitions receive more than 12,000 entries each year from organizations in more than 70 nations. Honoring organizations of all types and sizes, as well as the people behind them, the Stevies recognize outstanding workplace performance worldwide. Learn more at stevieawards.com

title: NEW JERSEY RESOURCES HOSTS 71st ANNUAL MEETING
body_text: New Jersey Resources NEW JERSEY RESOURCES HOSTS 71st ANNUAL MEETING 01/24/2024 - For Immediate Release Wall, NJ – New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR), today hosted its 71st Annual Shareowners Meeting. At the virtual meeting, shareowners elected Donald L. Correll, James H. DeGraffenreidt Jr., M. Susan Hardwick and Peter C. Harvey to NJR’s board of directors each for a three-year term that will expire in 2027. “I appreciate our shareowners overwhelming support for our directors and confidence in our company,” said Steve Westhoven, President and CEO of New Jersey Resources. “With the strong expertise of our board, we remain committed to executing on our growth strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareowners.” Also at the meeting, NJR’s longest serving independent director George R. Zoffinger retired from the board. Highly regarded for his leadership and extensive experience in business and government affairs, Mr. Zoffinger joined NJR’s board on May 9, 1996. During his tenure, he served as a member of the Audit Committee and Leadership Development and Compensation Committee, as well as Chair of the Nominating/Corporate Governance Committee, and contributed the growth and success of NJR. “I would like to thank George for his candor, counsel and contributions to our board and our company,” Mr. Westhoven said. “For 27 years, he served with distinction and helped make New Jersey Resources a better, stronger company.” In other business, shareowners approved a non-binding advisory resolution on the compensation of NJR’s named executive officers and ratified the appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as its independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2024. About New Jersey Resources New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a Fortune 1000 company that, through its subsidiaries, provides safe and reliable natural gas and clean energy services, including transportation, distribution, asset management and home services. NJR is composed of five primary businesses: New Jersey Natural Gas, NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve nearly 576,000 customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean and parts of Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties. Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects with a total capacity of approximately 469 megawatts, providing residential and commercial customers with low-carbon solutions. Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America. Storage and Transportation serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River Energy Center and the Adelphia Gateway Pipeline, as well as our 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility. Home Services provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators, solar and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homes throughout New Jersey. NJR and its over 1,300 employees are committed to helping customers save energy and money by promoting conservation and encouraging efficiency through Conserve to Preserve® and initiatives such as SAVEGREEN™ and The Sunlight Advantage®. For more information about NJR: www.njresources.com Follow us on X (formerly Twitter) @NJNaturalGas . “Like” us on facebook.com/NewJerseyNaturalGas . title: American Horsepower Prevails Again At The 2026 Dakar Rally as Brock Heger and Max Eddy Jr. Score Back-to-Back Wins, Delivering Polaris' Third Straight SSV Victory
summary: LOEB FrayMédia Motorsport - RZR Factory Racing Defend Dakar with Race-Ready Polaris RZR Pro R Rally, Engineered to Meet New FIA Regulations While Delivering Unmatched Power, Durability & Precision Handling.
body_text: 1/20/2026 American Horsepower Prevails Again At The 2026 Dakar Rally as Brock Heger and Max Eddy Jr. Score Back-to-Back Wins, Delivering Polaris' Third Straight SSV Victory LOEB FrayMédia Motorsport - RZR Factory Racing Defend Dakar with Race-Ready Polaris RZR Pro R Rally, Engineered to Meet New FIA Regulations While Delivering Unmatched Power, Durability & Precision Handling MINNEAPOLIS, MN (January 19, 2026) – After covering nearly 5,000 kilometers (3,045 miles) across 13 grueling stages, Polaris' RZR Factory Racing program, in partnership with LOEB FrayMédia Motorsport (LFM), again dominated the Side-by-Side (SSV) class with a third consecutive overall victory at the 48th running of the 2026 Dakar Rally. In their second showing at the event, the all-American duo of Brock Heger and navigator Max Eddy Jr. returned to the Saudi Arabian desert and once again delivered a masterclass in precision and endurance, earning their second consecutive class win behind the wheel of the dominant Polaris RZR Pro R Rally race machine , designed to meet the new FIA rule changes. Widely regarded as the most demanding race in the world, this year’s Dakar saw Heger and Eddy lead nearly the entire 13-stage event, ultimately claiming victory by over an hour. In only his second showing at the event, Heger once again delivered a historic performance, securing an unprecedented six stage victories, including the prologue. In addition, Heger finished on the podium two more times, earned two additional top-five results, and only finished outside the top five just four times throughout the entire event. Adding to Polaris’ remarkable performance, SLR teammate and 2024 SSV champion Xavier de Soultrait, also piloting a RZR Pro R Rally, rounded out the podium with a third-place overall finish. “ Coming back to Dakar for my second year and being able to win again is absolutely incredible, and I could not be more grateful for Polaris, LFM and our entire crew,” said Brock Heger . “This race pushes you in every possible way, and to come out on top again is something I’m really proud of. Max and I work seamlessly together. His navigation was spot on from start to finish, and that trust and communication between us made all the difference over two demanding weeks. The RZR Pro R Rally performed flawlessly every single day. It’s a machine that’s truly unmatched, and it just keeps getting better and better. Having a vehicle you can trust completely at Dakar is everything, and Polaris delivered exactly that.” Heger made an immediate statement for the second consecutive year by winning the prologue, securing a critical advantage heading into Stage 1. When the competition officially kicked off, teammate Xavier de Soultrait showcased his experience as the reigning 2024 Dakar winner, driving flawlessly to claim the Stage 1 victory and take the early overall lead. De Soultrait continued his strong run in Stage 2 with a second-place finish, while Heger placed fifth, maintaining De Soultrait’s advantage in the standings. From Stage 3 onward, Heger and Eddy shifted into command, capturing back-to-back stage wins to seize the overall lead. From that point forward, the duo never looked back, methodically guiding their Polaris RZR Pro R Rally through the unforgiving Saudi Arabian desert. Heger went on to claim additional stage victories in Stages 8, 10, and 11, while adding a third-place finish in Stage 5 and a fourth-place result in Stage 7, cementing a commanding and consistent performance from start to finish. The standout performance underscored the precision engineering of the Polaris RZR Pro R Rally, which delivered the reliability, power, and agility required to conquer Dakar’s treacherous terrain. When the dust settled, Heger and Eddy completed the marathon rally in 55 hours, 11 minutes, and 56 seconds, more than four hours faster than last year’s winning time. With new FIA regulations in place for the SSV class, Polaris engineered the RZR Pro R Rally to meet stringent homologation requirements while preserving the race-winning performance and durability that define the platform. Built around a largely stock-based chassis and bodywork, the vehicle retains key production RZR Pro R components, including the engine, driveline, and suspension, highlighting the inherent strength of the consumer platform. Enhanced suspension control and precise handling allow the RZR Pro R Rally to conquer the harshest terrain mile after mile, delivering the reliability, endurance, and performance required to secure victory in the world’s most demanding rally conditions. “To kick off the new year with a third consecutive Dakar Rally victory is truly an incredible achievement for both Polaris and Loeb FrayMedia Motorsport,” said Alex Scheuerell, Polaris’ Director of Off-Road Motorsports. “This partnership has been the recipe for dominance at Dakar, and to come away victorious again is incredibly rewarding. Because of the new rule changes in the SSV class, the team spent countless days and nights over the past year refining and evolving our platform. Seeing Brock and Max deliver another virtually flawless performance, along with Xavier securing a third-place finish on the podium, is a true testament to that hard work. They overcame some of the most intense conditions imaginable, and I can’t thank everyone at Polaris and LFM enough for the dedication and effort that made this victory possible.” In addition to Heger’s victory and De Soultrait’s third-place finish, the crew of Johan Kristoffersson and navigator Ola Fløene delivered a strong performance behind the wheel of the RZR Pro R Factory T4, finishing eighth overall in Kristoffersson’s first Dakar Rally appearance. The duo recorded three podium stage finishes along with an additional top-five result. Florent Vayssade’s rally was highlighted by a second-place finish in Stage 2, while young driver Gonçalo Guerreiro and navigator Maykel Justo put together an impressive and consistent run, earning one stage victory, two podium finishes, and three additional top-five stage results before being forced to retire following Stage 8 after a collision with another racer. Collectively, these performances showcased the depth, strength, and unity of the Polaris and Loeb FrayMédia Motorsports, reinforcing their dominance at one of the most demanding motorsport events in the world. To learn more, please visit Polaris.com/RZR or join the conversation and follow on Facebook , Instagram , YouTube and X . To follow the Loeb FrayMédia Motorsports team, check them out on Instagram . About Polaris As the global leader in powersports, Polaris Inc. (NYSE: PII) pioneers product breakthroughs and enriching experiences and services that have invited people to discover the joy of being outdoors since our founding in 1954. Polaris’ high-quality product line-up includes the RANGER, RZR and Polaris XPEDITION and GENERAL side-by-side off-road vehicles; Sportsman all-terrain off-road vehicles; military and commercial off-road vehicles; snowmobiles; Indian Motorcycle mid-size and heavyweight motorcycles; Slingshot moto-roadsters; Aixam quadricycles; Goupil electric vehicles; and pontoon and deck boats, including industry-leading Bennington pontoons. Polaris enhances the riding experience with a robust portfolio of parts, garments, and accessories.
